filename: HISTORY-BASED, BAYESIAN, CLOSURE FOR STOCHASTIC PARAMETERIZATION_ APPLICATION TO LORENZ ’96.pdf
title: History-based, Bayesian, Closure for Stochastic Parameterization: Application to Lorenz '96
parameterization_target: subgrid coupling term in Lorenz '96 system representing unresolved fast variables
testbed_rationale: Uses an idealized, low-dimensional toy model (Lorenz '96) rather than realistic Earth system, climate, or weather data/models, so it is not a direct candidate for the Earth Well benchmark dataset testbed.
pain_points: High computational cost of standard MCMC in high-dimensional neural network parameter spaces.
Temporal discretization errors and numerical stability issues when using coarse time steps in online integration.
Absence of information on unobserved fast/subgrid variables causing non-Markovian memory effects and stochastic mismatch.
Observational noise and temporal sparsity in data causing parameter and forecast uncertainty.
extraction_notes: The study demonstrates a delay-differential equation (history-based) parameterization using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling within JAX for the Lorenz '96 system.
